article.Citation/Title: Pahnke, W. N., Kurland, A. A., Unger, S., Savage, C., & Grof, S. (1970). The experimental use of psychedelic (LSD) psychotherapy. JAMA, 212(11), 1856-1863.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Pahnke, W. N., Kurland, A. A., Unger, S., Savage, C., & Grof, S. (1970). The experimental use of psychedelic (LSD) psychotherapy.pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Oral LSD, single session: high dose 350-450ug vs low-dose 50ug active comparator; ~20 hours preparatory psychotherapy, 10-12 hour drug session with therapist/nurse, follow-up integration therapy; inpatient hospital treatment suite.

ae_events.Description: Persisting psychological disturbance in the days following the LSD session, in two patients, requiring subsequent conventional psychiatric treatment.

article.Outcome: Article contains no structured abstract or explicit primary-outcome statement; per precedence rule 2 (SUD-behavioral outcome), 'Drinking Behavior' is used over 'Global Adjustment'. Within Drinking Behavior, Table 2 gives the authors' own dichotomized 'rigorous criterion' (0-10 scale score of 8-10, i.e., near-total abstinence) as a two-group high-vs-low dose comparison for the N=104 single-LSD-session cohort: High dose 53% (34/64) vs Low dose 33% (13/40). Chosen over the continuous Table 1 ANCOVA means (F=4.43, p<0.025) because the task instructions specifically direct that a high-vs-low-dose two-group proportion be captured as 'X% vs Y%' with OR computed from the counts; see config_proposal.
article.SD: Table 2 has a companion 'Results For Above Data' F/p row for this exact percentage comparison, but the OCR/column conversion interleaves it with unrelated case-report prose ('...low dose 005 344 O05...Psychedelic reactivity groups 7.74 0.025 3.07 significant...'), and the row/column alignment cannot be reconstructed without inferring a substitution rule, which is prohibited. Coded '.' rather than guessed. Table 1's clean, unambiguous ANCOVA F=4.43 (p<0.025) is for the continuous drinking-behavior score, a related but distinct analysis from the % criterion used in Outcome, so it is not substituted in per the 'not a different analysis's statistic' rule.
article.PVal: Same garbling issue as SD: the Table 2 significance test paired with the 53% vs 33% comparison is not reliably legible. Coded '.' rather than reusing Table 1's p<0.025 (continuous-score analysis, not the % criterion).
article.SampleSize_NFinal: N=104 is the sum of the two dosage-arm N's in Tables 1 and 2 (High N=64 + Low N=40), the subset of the 117 single-LSD-session patients who were personally located for the 6-month follow-up interview (13 of 117 were lost to follow-up).

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective, setting (Spring Grove/Maryland Psychiatric Research Center), intervention doses, active comparator, outcome scales, randomization (2/3 allotted high dose), double-blind design, ANCOVA statistics, results tables, a dedicated safety section, and NIMH funding/Sandoz LSD-supply disclosure are all described. No inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond 'alcoholic patients' are stated, and no power calculation or sample-size justification is discussed. 12 of 14 met, below the 13-criterion threshold, so MethodologyDescribedYN = 0.

article.Retention (%): Denominator is 117 (patients with a single LSD session, the analytic subgroup used for Tables 1-2; the 18 patients with >1 session were excluded from this subgroup for uniformity of treatment amount, not attrition). Of these 117, 104 were personally located for the 6-month follow-up interview (13 lost). 104/117 = 88.9%.
article.Comparator: The 'control' group received an active low dose of LSD (50ug) with identical therapeutic preparation to the high-dose (350-450ug) group -- an active dose-comparison, not a placebo control. Coded Comparator=1 per the dose-comparison rule.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: No explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria are enumerated for the 135-patient alcoholism trial beyond the diagnosis label 'alcoholic patients'; coded 0.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Global Adjustment and Drinking Behavior were rated on a 'predetermined 0 to 10 behavior rating scale' devised for this research program by an independent evaluation team; no citation to an established/validated psychometric instrument (e.g., AUDIT, ASI) is given, so coded 0.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: No description of how the 135-patient cohort was recruited (screened volunteers vs. broader referral base) is given; a separate, smaller substudy elsewhere in the article describes '82 consecutive alcoholic patients' but that group is not clearly the same as the 135/117/104 cohort analyzed in Tables 1-2, so representativeness could not be established and this was coded 0.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Spring Grove State Hospital and the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Baltimore, Maryland, United States.
article.Followup in months: The independent rating team's protocol specifies assessment at 6, 12, and 18 months, but the article states 'Results are now completed at the six-month checkpoint... Full and final analysis and evaluation of these data are still in progress' -- only 6-month outcome data are actually reported in Tables 1-2, so Followup in months reflects the reported horizon (6), not the full planned protocol (18).
article.MortalityMeasured: One death is reported in the article (an illustrative case-report patient who died of surgical complications), but that patient was enrolled in a separate cancer-pain pilot project described elsewhere in the same article, not in the 135-patient alcoholism trial that is the subject of this Alcohol-condition extraction. No mortality outcome is reported for the alcoholism cohort itself, so coded 0.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Chromosomal aberration rate (a biomarker) was measured before/after LSD administration in 32 patients treated at Spring Grove State Hospital (Table 3); the article does not explicitly confirm these 32 are drawn from the 135-patient alcoholism cohort, but Spring Grove was the site of the alcoholism trial, so this is treated as a physical/biological outcome measured within the study program.

ae_events.Pahnke 1970_AE01: The article's safety statement ('over 300 patients have been treated with LSD... although there have been two cases in which disturbances persisted in the days following the actual LSD session. Both patients subsequently responded to conventional psychiatric treatment') is a pooled statement spanning the whole Spring Grove/Maryland Psychiatric Research Center LSD program (alcoholic, neurotic, and narcotic-addict patients), not broken out for the 135-alcoholic-patient trial specifically -- hence AE_denominator = 'Not numbered' rather than 104 or 300, and ArmScope = psychedelic_arm since both the high- and low-dose arms received active LSD (no placebo-only comparator exists to pool against). Graded Moderate because the described consequence (persisting disturbance requiring subsequent psychiatric treatment) meets the rubric's active-intervention/persistence-beyond-dosing-day threshold but no hospitalization, life-threatening course, or author-assigned SAE/serious label is stated. SeveritySource=rubric because the authors used only descriptive language ('disturbances persisted'), not a formal severity or seriousness label of their own. Excluded from this article's AE data: the transient in-session apprehension/confusion/paranoia and post-treatment death described in the illustrative case report, because that patient belonged to a separate cancer-pain pilot project, not the alcoholism trial.

config_proposal.note: High-dose LSD (350-450ug) vs low-dose LSD (50ug) comparison of the percentage of alcoholic patients meeting the authors' 'rehabilitated' drinking-behavior criterion (0-10 scale score of 8-10) at 6-month follow-up (Table 2, N=104). OR computed directly from the reported 2x2 counts; coded 'approx' rather than 'clean' because converting a dichotomized-scale proportion to an odds ratio involves an assumption a methodologist would want to review, and because the article's own paired significance test for this specific comparison is illegibly garbled in the source conversion.
